text: In nineteen eighty-five, Britain was promised the electric car of the future. It was a battery tricycle with a top speed of twenty-four kilometres an hour. The Sinclair C5 sat you just above the road, open to the rain, and safety experts worried lorry drivers would never even see you. One small motor and one lead-acid battery. In the cold the battery faded, and on hills the motor overheated. So you pedalled. It was built in a Hoover washing machine factory. Sales collapsed within months, and the company was in receivership by October. Dave took it on the motorway.
